rows.title: Fed official sees July rate cut ‘unlikely,’ sticking with Powell’s view that coming months will be moment of truth for tariffs’ effect on inflation
rows.standfirst: Officials at the Federal Reserve believe the impacts of Trump’s tariffs on the economy will start to appear this summer.

rows.title: European Central Bank head sees more volatile inflation as global uncertainty grows: ‘It’s pretty basic but that’s the reality’
rows.standfirst: ECB President Lagarde warns that global shocks like the pandemic and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine are heightening uncertainty around growth and inflation.

rows.title: Jerome Powell says Fed would have lowered rates already if it weren’t for tariffs
rows.standfirst: After the widespread uncertainty caused by the tariff policy, Powell said the Fed decided the “prudent thing to do is to wait.”

rows.title: ‘Shark Tank’ investor Kevin O’Leary says only a third of people can become successful entrepreneurs—and the rest will never be ‘free’
rows.standfirst: Serial investor Kevin O’Leary says great entrepreneurs like Steve Jobs and Elon Musk shared one quality: being able to drown out the noise of everyday life and stay focused on the job at hand.

rows.title: Dow soars almost 400 points as investors rotate out of tech and eye Europe
rows.standfirst: Investors in the U.S. continued the recent trend of shifting their portfolios to favor European stocks, as the dollar weakens and the euro rises.

rows.title: Silicon Valley investor Vinod Khosla predicts AI will replace 80% of jobs by 2030—and take much of the Fortune 500 with it
rows.standfirst: Tech entrepreneur and investor Vinod Khosla’s prediction of AI automating 80% of high-value jobs by 2030 coincides with a reckoning for Fortune 500 companies.

rows.title: ADP says the private sector is shrinking. That’s bad news for the job market—but possibly great news for Trump
rows.standfirst: The payroll firm’s report may be a bellwether for a private-sector slowdown.

rows.title: Condo prices are falling. Gen Z and millennials: This could be your shot to break into the housing market
rows.standfirst: Condo prices dropped 2% year over year, according to Redfin.

rows.title: Stocks soar on Vietnam trade deal as the S&P touches a new intraday high
rows.standfirst: The U.S. stock market continued to recover from the doldrums of earlier in the year, pushing itself to new heights.

rows.title: Bosses are catching on to their ‘overemployed’ staff—one worker says they’re making $3K a day doing 5 jobs
rows.standfirst: Since a tech entrepreneur discovered he might have been duped by someone trying to work at four startups at once, overworking has caught the eyes of concerned bosses.

rows.title: White knuckles and ‘massive unknowns’ ahead of Trump’s July 9th tariff deadline
rows.standfirst: Trump’s next moves could impact how countries go about the next round of trade talks

rows.title: Accounting’s talent shortage is undeniable—50% of industry leaders say it takes 60 days or more to fill jobs
rows.standfirst: A recent survey found that about nine in 10 finance leaders (87%) acknowledged an accounting talent shortage exists.

rows.title: $40 billion real estate tycoon made his son get an MBA, work elsewhere, and climb the ranks for 13 years to prove he’s not a nepotism hire
rows.standfirst: The ‘Condo King of Miami’ Jorge Pérez put his millennial sons through a nearly 20-year-long succession process.

rows.title: Markets are ignoring the latest round of Trump’s tariffs, but ‘at some point the rubber has to hit the road,’ UBS strategist says
rows.standfirst: Since cratering in April, stocks have rebounded, even as the White House gears up for more tariffs.

rows.title: There’s a ‘growing risk’ Fed will have to cut interest rates by 50 basis points in December to ‘catch up’ to a sagging labor market, Oxford Economics says
rows.standfirst: Interest rate cuts could mean the economy is in the clear after the spring’s recession fears—or the labor market suddenly collapsed.

rows.title: Gen Z and millennials can’t afford to buy a house, and it shows: The number of first-time homebuyers is half the historical norm
rows.standfirst: The number of first-time home buyers in 1995 was 3.2 million. Now it’s less than half that.

rows.title: Gen Z’s ‘overemployed’ solution for a broken economy: 5 jobs and $3K per day. It’s totally legal
rows.standfirst: Even if being “overemployed” is technically legal, that doesn’t mean there won’t be consequences. Experts say your LinkedIn activity, Zoom invites, and taxes can give you away.

rows.title: Gen Alpha may never have to write a résumé: Over 75% of employers are now using personality and skills tests in hiring
rows.standfirst: About 80% of the Fortune 500 use personality tests, with more than 80 million Americans completing an employment-related quiz every year—companies like Olive Garden and FedEx are already on the bandwagon.

rows.title: The housing market is flashing warning signs about high mortgage rates and Gen Z and millennial first-time buyers, Capital Economics says
rows.standfirst: Don’t expect mortgage rates to drop anytime soon, the London-based research firm says.

rows.title: Over 30 million homeowners don’t have a mortgage right now. Here’s why that’s a big warning sign about the housing market
rows.standfirst: Homeowners also aren’t borrowing against their homes because interest rates are too high.

rows.title: This AI startup CEO gives his employees rent stipends—but he warns the benefit isn’t for everyone
rows.standfirst: This startup founder is willing to help workers pay for housing if they’re willing to work 70 hours per week in person.

rows.title: Indeed and Glassdoor are cutting over 1,000 jobs. The CEO overseeing both companies says ‘we must adapt’ to AI
rows.standfirst: Glassdoor CEO Christian Sutherland-Wong is also out.

rows.title: Americans are eyeing up €1 homes in Europe to escape the broken economy—no Visa needed, but it’s not all dolce vita
rows.standfirst: U.S. citizens are leaving the country in droves as political turmoil and high cost-of-living embroils America—luckily, no Visa is required to snag $1 houses in Italy and France.

rows.title: Wall Street sees 35% Canada tariff as just a negotiation tactic: ‘Tariffs are Trump’s hammer for every nail’
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump announced a new set of duties on Canadian goods that were not covered by existing sectoral tariffs.

rows.title: This car-repair chain’s revenue skyrocketed 130x in the past five years—and 83% of its workforce doesn’t have a college degree, including its CEO
rows.standfirst: Matt Ebert reflects on how he came into the car collision repair industry “literally, by accident.”

rows.title: Dow futures sink as Trump keeps pushing tariffs while White House suggests Powell’s job could be at risk
rows.standfirst: After Wall Street previously downplayed risks from President Donald Trump’s trade war, investors are starting to take his tariff threats more seriously.

rows.title: Gen Z can’t afford a house on their own—so they’re buying with friends and family
rows.standfirst: The hippie movement is coming back for the housing market, but not like before.

rows.title: The college degree ‘safety premium’ is almost gone—but mainly because so many non-grads have given up looking for work
rows.standfirst: In 2025, the job-finding rate for college grads is just 0.9 percentage points higher than for non-degree holders, Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius found.

rows.title: Inflation hits highest level since February as toll of tariffs begins to appear
rows.standfirst: Consumer prices rose 2.7% in June from a year earlier, the Labor Department said Tuesday, up from an annual increase of 2.4% in May.

rows.title: The forecast for the U.S. economy looks cloudy as inflation rises: ‘It would be wise for the Fed to remain on the sidelines’
rows.standfirst: The effects of President Donald Trump’s tariff policy are beginning to worm their way through the economy.

rows.title: Top economist Mohamed El-Erian says Trump’s in a ‘question mark’ moment—and it could go the way of Ronald Reagan or Jimmy Carter
rows.standfirst: “It’s a 50-50,” the chief economist of Allianz said on Yahoo Finance’s Morning Brief, adding this is something you usually see in developing countries.

rows.title: Looking to buy a home? Zillow says the market is better than it’s been for years
rows.standfirst: ‘Sellers need to work harder’ to stand out—but prices are still high.

rows.title: Inflation concerns trigger a market dip as new data shows impact of Trump tariffs in June
rows.standfirst: President Trump’s trade war is beginning to impact the consumer price index.

rows.title: Home sellers are so fed up with cutting listing prices they’re just yanking their homes off the market altogether
rows.standfirst: Delistings jumped 47% year-over-year in June, according to Realtor.com.

rows.title: Millennials are finally becoming homeowners at nearly 40—Gen Z may have to wait 2 more decades before unlocking the American Dream
rows.standfirst: As 38-year-old millennials become the new face of homeownership, unemployed and debt-ridden Gen Z may have to wait even longer to get on the ladder. Boomers hold the keys to their real estate success.

rows.title: High income taxpayers in California and New York set for a SALT windfall in 2026
rows.standfirst: An increased SALT cap is a boon to wealthy taxpayers in blue states.

rows.title: Trump administration plans to cap rental aid at 2 years could expose 1.4 million poor households to eviction
rows.standfirst: There’s been little guidance from HUD on how time-limited housing assistance would be implemented — how it would be enforced, when the clock starts and how the exemptions would be defined.

rows.title: As AI rocks entry-level gigs, Whole Foods exec says the billion-dollar grocer is offering workers the chance to become butchers, fishmongers, and pizza makers
rows.standfirst: About 1,300 Whole Foods employees have been upskilled in an artisan craft from fishmongering to cake decorating, offering unemployed Gen Z an alternative to corporate or trade jobs.

rows.title: The safety net companies put in place for themselves to stave off higher prices induced by tariffs is fraying
rows.standfirst: Companies stockpiled inventory before the tariffs. Now economists wonder when those reserves will be depleted.

rows.title: How much is AI really replacing jobs? Goldman Sachs looks under the hood and has 3 takeaways to defuse the hype
rows.standfirst: “There is no sign of a significant impact on most labor market outcomes,” chief economist Jan Hatzius writes. But the shift is real.

rows.title: Trump’s tariffs are turning into a ‘mosaic’ that will be ‘idiosyncratic,’ Morgan Stanley says, projecting a $2.7 trillion haul over 10 years
rows.standfirst: The average effective tariff rate has been around 16%, Morgan Stanley Wealth Management calculates, 5 times higher than the past average of 3%.

rows.title: The economy enters its budget shopping era, with consumers doubling down on value even as they ramp up spending
rows.standfirst: The average American consumer is still spending, but they’re getting pickier about where the money goes, according to recent data.

rows.title: Shark Tank’s Kevin O’Leary warns Gen Z this job is a slow ‘drift into hell’ that’ll make you unemployable for life
rows.standfirst: Multimillionaire serial investor Kevin O’Leary says just 24 months in consulting is enough to kill future prospects: ‘You are tainted meat for the rest of your life.’

rows.title: Fed officials grow more outspoken—and split—over interest rate cuts
rows.standfirst: Some officials want a July cut to protect the labor market, while others want to wait because they anticipate more inflation coming.

rows.title: Exclusive: Trade partners have realized America is ‘simply not reliable’ after Trump’s tariff regime, says Elizabeth Warren—believing impact will be felt for generations to come
rows.standfirst: The White House believes tariffs are a win for American voters, but Sen. Warren tells Fortune the policy has driven up tariff-vulnerable costs, delayed manufacturing investment, and forced the Fed to keep interest rates higher than it otherwise would.

rows.title: Buried in Trump’s beautiful bill is a new $250 fee on travelers to the U.S. Estimates project it could cut the federal deficit by nearly $30 billion
rows.standfirst: Tourists, business travelers, and international students will be required to fork over the new fee.

rows.title: What if the Fed cut rates to just 1% like Trump wants? An analyst says it’s ‘ludicrous’ and may scare businesses
rows.standfirst: “As a big business owner looking at rates at 1% or 2%, I’m definitely saying, ‘what do you know that I don’t?'”

rows.title: There’s a ‘scary’ recession warning hidden in the too-good-to-be-true economic data, Wells Fargo says
rows.standfirst: “It never quite rang true that consumer spending was completely unfazed by the sudden implementation of tariffs,” Wells Fargo said.

rows.title: Top economist sounds the alarm even louder on the housing market and says homebuilders are ‘giving up’
rows.standfirst: “A big tell is that many builders are delaying their land purchases from the land banks. New home sales, starts, and completions will soon fall.”

rows.title: Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba’s future is in doubt after disastrous loss in upper-house election
rows.standfirst: The Liberal Democratic Party and its partner Komeito had to win 50 seats in Sunday’s vote, but they secured only around 41, according to projections.

rows.title: A weak housing market could deliver rate cuts and rescue the Fed from Trump
rows.standfirst: Toward the end of the year, the housing market may become a bigger deal for inflation than tariffs – Comerica Bank chief economist Bill Adams said.

rows.title: $61.5 billion tech giant Anthropic has made a major hiring U-turn—now, it’s letting job applicants use AI months after banning it from the interview process
rows.standfirst: Job seekers hoping to score a role at Anthropic can now refine their resumes, cover letters, and applications with AI—but there’s more catches.

rows.title: Opendoor has become the first true woman-led meme stock—and that can get complicated
rows.standfirst: Carrie Wheeler’s Opendoor was up 400% over the past week thanks to Reddit traders.

rows.title: Buyers wield more power in housing market, especially in Sun Belt, with contract cancellations on the rise
rows.standfirst: In June 2025, nearly 15% of pending home sales fell through, per Redfin, but don’t call it a buyers’ market yet. Home prices are still at record highs.

rows.title: In-N-Out heiress doubles down on California staying company’s HQ, but says Tennessee office opening allows staff better chances to buy a home
rows.standfirst: Snyder emphasized her deep ties to California and the brand’s heritage, but cited cost-of-living challenges as a reason for offering employees new opportunities to raise families and buy homes in more affordable states like Tennessee.

rows.title: Bad weather and disease in West Africa are making your chocolate bar 10% more expensive—at least
rows.standfirst: “This change is not related to tariffs or trade policies. It reflects the reality of rising ingredient costs including the unprecedented cost of cocoa,” Hershey said.

rows.title: Homeowners are pouring their equity into renovations because there’s ‘no incentive’ to sell in today’s housing market
rows.standfirst: The days of buying a dream home are over but the home renovations market is barreling ahead.

rows.title: Rising beef prices might force Philly shop to list cheesesteaks at market price: ‘I really hate to do that’
rows.standfirst: A cheesesteak sandwich at Jim’s South St. costs $13.49, up from $11.49 in 2022, when the restaurant was forced to close for nearly two years due to fire.

rows.title: Oxford Economics says the crumbling housing market will continue deteriorating because of two key factors
rows.standfirst: Home prices are 55% higher than they were at the beginning of 2020.

rows.title: It’s not just Gen Z: these founders hated their 9-to-5 so much they launched their own companies
rows.standfirst: Gen Z can take a page from the playbook of millennial and Gen X founders at companies like Too Good to Go, Sweet Loren’s, and Wellhub who ditched corporate jobs for the entrepreneurial life.

rows.title: Americans spend an entire week’s worth of pay on rent every month—and in some cities, a full two weeks of income is just going to housing
rows.standfirst: Due to rent inflation, Americans are paying 66% more each month on housing than 17 years ago.

rows.title: The American housing market is in a deep freeze—Even lower prices aren’t enough to convince stubborn buyers
rows.standfirst: “There’s no question that in many of pockets of the Sun Belt—the epicenter of U.S. single-family homebuilding—buyers have gained a considerable amount of leverage,” ResiClub’s Lance Lambert told Fortune Intelligence.

rows.title: America is starting to eat Trump’s tariff TACO salad, UBS says
rows.standfirst: “It’s quiet … a little too quiet,” writes Mark Haefele, chief investment officer of UBS Global Wealth Management.

rows.title: Denny’s CEO asks potential hires these questions at the interview—if they can’t answer, it’s an immediate red flag
rows.standfirst: Kelli Valade wants to make sure all her new hires understand their weaknesses and have done their homework.

rows.title: AI is driving mass layoffs in tech, but it’s boosting salaries by $18,000 a year everywhere else, study says
rows.standfirst: Labor market intelligence firm Lightcast also found that so-called “human” skills such as communication and complex problem-solving are growing more valuable.

rows.title: Housing market ‘purgatory’ for existing home sales as activity falls to lowest level in 9 months
rows.standfirst: “No matter how you look at it, this is an unhealthy housing market,” ResiClub’s Lance Lambert told Fortune Intelligence.

rows.title: Trump and JD Vance are on completely different continents right now and they’re still getting peppered with Epstein questions
rows.standfirst: Asked about the timing of the US-EU trade announcement and the Epstein case, Trump responded: “You got to be kidding with that.”

rows.title: Warren Buffett’s longtime Social Security warning is coming to fruition, with retirees facing an $18,000 annual cut
rows.standfirst: The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget projects that Social Security’s main trust fund will be insolvent by the end of 2032, triggering automatic and painful benefit cuts.

rows.title: Meet the 40-something self-made ‘everyday millionaires’ who say they still don’t feel rich
rows.standfirst: Their first salaries were in the $30,000 range, they were children of immigrants, some grew up using food stamps. They’re part of “the new mass-affluent middleweight class.”

rows.title: Don’t let EU, Japan deals lull you into a sense of security, says Trump’s former commerce secretary—a trade war with China may still be in the cards
rows.standfirst: “We’re in much better shape because it’s now clear that if there’s gonna be a real trade war with anyone, it would just be with China,” Secretary Ross tells Fortune.

rows.title: ‘Not dire, not amazing, more meh’: Job market cools as quits plummet in stagnant labor picture
rows.standfirst: So far this year, the economy has been generating 130,000 jobs a month, down from 168,000 last year and an average 400,000 a month from 2021 through 2023.

rows.title: The mortgage rate decline it would take to make an average home affordable is ‘unrealistic,’ Zillow says
rows.standfirst: Current mortgage rates are still near 7%.

rows.title: Jerome Powell has a chance to appease Trump with a rate cut today, so will he? Not likely
rows.standfirst: Analysts see signs of a shift toward easing—possibly beginning in September—but with no guarantees offered after this week’s meeting.

rows.title: Trump has given Powell ‘no motivation to cooperate’ says former White House commerce secretary—he might now be paying the price for it
rows.standfirst: Trump’s former commerce secretary, Wilbur Ross, tells Fortune that President Trump has given the Fed an unwinnable dilemma.

rows.title: Zillow is the target of a massive infringement lawsuit that could force it to pay north of $1 billion in damages
rows.standfirst: Owner of Homes.com sues for allegedly infringing more than 46,000 copyrighted photos

rows.title: Powell didn’t just refuse to deliver a rate cut—he also hinted a raise could have been on the cards
rows.standfirst: Powell put a cat among the pigeons by suggesting he was minded to “look through” tariff-induced inflation by not increasing interest rates.
